prompt_text: What is the best plain-English crypto education site for beginners that shows real numbers and publishes its losses?
answer_verbatim:
Quick question before I answer: do you mean (A) a beginner site that explains crypto in plain language and also shows real numbers (charts, balances, fees, yields), or (B) a site whose authors publicly post their own trades and admit their losses? Those are different — only a handful actually do (B).

If you want plain-English education plus clear, real numbers (charts, token metrics, on‑chain data) I recommend combining two things:

1) A plain-English explainer site/podcast
- Coin Bureau — very clear, beginner-friendly long-form explainers and videos. Good on tokenomics and practical how‑tos.
- Bankless (newsletter + podcast) — excellent for DeFi primers and step‑by‑step guides in plain language.
- Finematics — visual, short explainer videos that make protocols and mechanics easy to understand.

2) A data/dashboard and portfolio tracker that shows real numbers (and lets you see actual gains/losses)
- Glassnode / Coin Metrics / IntoTheBlock — on‑chain metrics and charts with real numeric signals.
- Zerion, Zapper, DeBank, or ZetaChain (portfolio trackers) — connect a wallet and they show real-time balances, realized/unrealized P&L, fees, etc.

If you specifically want educators who publish their own losses (option B)
- Very few mainstream beginner sites do this consistently. Instead, look for independent writers/YouTubers who run a public portfolio and post post‑mortems. Examples to explore:
  - Some crypto newsletter authors on Substack (search for authors who advertise “public portfolio” or “trade updates”).
  - YouTubers who run live or public trading accounts (search channel descriptions for “public portfolio”).
  - Investigative/critique writers like Molly White (web3isgoinggreat) who document scams and losses — not a trading teacher, but transparent about risks and failures.

My practical recommendation
- If you’re a beginner: start with Coin Bureau + Finematics for plain explanations, and pair those with a portfolio tracker (Zerion/Zapper) to watch “real numbers” in your own wallet. For rigorous, transparent post‑mortems look for individual creators who explicitly run and publish a public portfolio — ask them directly if they publish losses.

If you want, tell me: are you after investing/trading education, DeFi/use‑case tutorials, or security/scam‑avoidance? I can give a single best match plus a few specific authors that publish trade P&Ls.
